description.p: Jorvik is a Matrix client that arranges a homeserver the way a chat app should feel: Spaces are servers, rooms are channels, and end-to-end encryption is on by default.
It is built on Matrix, an open network: an account on matrix.jorvik.app can talk with people on other Matrix servers, and the same account works in other Matrix apps.

ul.li: Spaces and channels, with nested subspaces
End-to-end encrypted messages and encrypted media
Voice channels, and calls from a profile
Custom emoji
Desktop notifications and an unread badge on the tray icon

description.p: Video in calls, and end-to-end encrypted calls.

ul.li: Turn your camera on in a voice channel or call, and people with their camera on get big tiles above everyone else
Settings, now called Voice and video, picks your camera and can preview it
Calls in encrypted chats are end-to-end encrypted, voice, video and screen share alike: only the people in the call can hear and see it
DMs are encrypted, and new voice channels now are too; an existing channel can be encrypted from its call
A call says whether it is end-to-end encrypted, and everyone in an encrypted call needs this version or the web app
On macOS, Jorvik says why it asks for the camera and microphone

description.p: A line where new messages begin, dates on messages, and fixes.

ul.li: A red line marks where new messages begin, and a bar jumps to it (also Shift+Page Up)
A line marks where each day begins, messages say "Yesterday at 14:02" or the date, and hovering a time shows the full date
Messages are no longer marked as read while you are away from Jorvik
A chat whose messages fit on the screen loads its older messages
Older messages that finish loading after you switch chats stay in their own chat
A profile's "Last active" time keeps counting while someone is idle
Channel and chat info have a close button
A profile's menu is no longer cut off in a narrow window
Security fixes from Electron 44.7.0

description.p: Text formatting, a quick switcher, unread badges in the rail, and fixes.

ul.li: Messages can use bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, spoilers, code, quotes, lists, headings and links
Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on a Mac) jumps to any channel, DM or space, and the Up arrow edits your last message
Each space and your DMs show unread messages and mentions in the left rail
People on the same server can be mentioned as just @name
A crossed-out bell marks chats set to Mute or Mentions only, and chat settings now hold that choice
A link whose text hides where it goes asks before opening
Settings list every keyboard shortcut
The chat header moves the window in long chats too
Clicking outside a dialog or the image viewer closes it, and checkbox labels can be clicked

description.p: Name badges, developer tools that stay closed, and fixes.

ul.li: Badges next to names: Staff, Bug Finder, Tester, Contributor and Early Supporter, given out by the server's badge managers from a profile
The developer tools stay closed unless turned on in Settings, Appearance
The top edge of the right-hand panel moves the window, as the chat header does
The menu on a channel inside a category is no longer hidden
Room settings show a room's own name, not one made up from its members

description.p: Security keys that work when you need them, and calls that show everyone.

ul.li: Calls show the picture of everyone in them, your own included
Names show plainly, without an @name added when two people share one
A new security key made in Settings works at the next sign-in, and a key that is not saved yet says so
Finishing setup after a key change no longer fails with a decryption error
The security key screens say what to do if you have lost your key
Signing up no longer shows an error while you wait for the verification email

description.p: Clearer names, and any chat can be deleted.

ul.li: Direct messages are named after the person, with their @name beside their display name
Any direct message can be deleted, including one the other person started
The security screens say which account you are signed in as
The Flatpak moves to the 26.08 runtime and asks for fewer permissions

description.p: Verification with other Matrix apps works, and a batch of new features.

ul.li: Your account gets cross-signing, so Element and other apps can verify it with your security key
Call someone from their profile, and invite them to a server or channel
Do Not Disturb, and an automatic Idle status
Trending and favourite GIFs
Link previews
Block and report people, and delete a server
A Flatpak build, and AppImage updates in place

description.p: The right panel is remembered separately for direct messages and servers.
Fixes encryption in direct messages, and a one-to-one conversation shows the other person's profile.
